newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police find suspected IRA arms cache.
newsitem.headline: Irish police find suspected IRA arms cache.

text.p: Irish police said on Friday they had found a suspected IRA arms cache during a joint army-police search close to the border with Northern Ireland.
"At the moment we have a small number of firearms, assorted ammunition and some bomb-making equipment," a police spokesman said after the find near Hackballscross in County Monaghan.

Last month Irish police uncovered a store of mortar tubes, the favoured weapon of the Irish Republican Army guerrillas fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland. It was not known if the two finds were connected, police said.
The latest arms find was the third in six months, and follows a series of tips from the public about IRA activities, security sources said.
In June, the IRA killed an Irish policeman in a bungled robery in the southern village of Adare, an incident which outraged the government, opposition and ordinary people.
The IRA is thought to have up to 100 tonnes of arms, ammunition and explosives, most of it concealed in underground bunkers in Ireland.
